page: Vultr voc-s-16c-128gb-3840s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz, with 2 threads per core. The processor includes a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 128.0 GB, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled and consists of a 3840 GB NVMe SSD. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2912.97, placing it in the top 25% of tested instances. Multi-core CPU performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 46204.81 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10847.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show average throughput, measuring 123.94 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 70.41 GB/sec for large block write operations. In database operations, the instance achieves an average PassMark database score of 7168.29 and processes 28.04 million Redis SET operations per second. Large-model LLM inference is not supported, but the system handles medium-model text generation at 20.35 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high memory density and substantial local NVMe storage relative to its compute allocation, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads without the premium of specialized bare-metal hardware. However, the 2.0 GHz clock speed and average multi-core scaling represent a tradeoff for compute-bound tasks that require high-frequency processing. This configuration is suitable for database hosting, memory-cached web serving, software compilation, and moderate-scale data processing workloads.
